title: Session-floor negotiation with directional multipliers for hybrid streaming
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Summary:
Run a controlled pilot to test 'directional multipliers' (different weights for ingress vs egress tokens) combined with negotiable session-level soft minimums for enterprise customers using long-lived streaming sessions. This ticket owns experiment design, telemetry specs, legal/SQ checklist input, and ramp plan for 6 pilot accounts.

Goals:
- Measure whether applying a small multiplier to ingress tokens (0.8x–1.2x) and egress tokens (0.8x–1.4x) improves perceived fairness for customers with hallucination-prone outputs and unbalanced IO patterns.
- Validate session-floor behavior (soft minimums that can be negotiated in contract) and observe churn/usage elasticity when floors are applied vs waived.
- Ensure meters and billing pipeline correctly attribute multi-turn streaming to ingress/egress buckets and report in Console per-route breakdowns.

Hypothesis:
- Directional multipliers with transparent per-session reporting will reduce billing complaints for customers with high-output use cases while preserving host revenue for outbound-heavy workloads.

Success criteria (primary):
- <10% of pilot customers raise billing disputes in first 45 days.
- No more than 3% increase in average per-token latency after instrumentation changes.
- Telemetry shows stable split attribution (ingress:egress ratio) with <2% variance between reported and raw metered tokens.

Scope and exclusions:
- Scope: Hosted API (text generation and chat streaming only). Include streaming SDKs and Console telemetry. Implement multiplier logic in billing calculation layer only; do not change customer-visible per-token pricing in public docs.
- Exclusions: Dedicated/Dedicated Reserved contracts and Private deployments are out of scope for this pilot.

Experiment design:
- 6 pilot customers (3 outbound-heavy, 3 inbound-heavy) with negotiated soft minimums: two variants for soft minimum window (monthly & 30-day rolling).
- Run 45-day blind pilot where customers see their effective session-floor and per-route breakdown but invoice reflects existing public rates; we simulate 'invoiced floor vs effective floor' to capture behavioral signals.
- Implement directional multipliers as configurable flags per customer: default multiplier set = {ingress:1.0, egress:1.15}.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- Add per-session attribution metrics: session_id, ingress_tokens, egress_tokens, multiplier_applied (string), effective_billed_tokens, effective_billed_amount.
- Dashboard: /console/dashboards/pricing/PM-808881-session-floor (internal).
- Create anomaly alerts for >5% discrepancy between raw meter and effective billed tokens.

Legal / Security questionnaire (SQ) path:
- Prepare text for Enterprise SQ describing: "No payloads are retained beyond policy; billing attribution operates on token counts only; floors are contractual credits applied on invoice reconciliation." Attachances include redlined language for sales/finance.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Customers misunderstand simulated billing leading to churn. Mitigation: Clear comms, CSM triage, and opt-out button.
- Risk: Billing pipeline regression. Mitigation: Staging end-to-end test, canary 1 customer before full pilot.

Next steps (high level):
- Finalize telemetry event schema (PM -> ENG) and schedule canary.
- Legal to review SQ language and draft contract addendum for soft minimums.
- Prepare internal runbook for disputes during pilot.

Notes and links:
- Experiment design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIC/PM-808881+Directional+IO+Session+Floors
- Telemetry spec (spreadsheet): https://drive.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-example-spec
- Draft contract language (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-example-contracts
